---

A lesson marks each statement that a reader could take for a scientific
result as a claim and gives it a type: observational, experimentally
supported, numerically verified, or formal theorem. The type says what kind of
evidence stands behind the statement. This page lists every claim of the
site, lesson by lesson, with its scope and the evidence it names. The claim
links to its place in the lesson. The evidence is one of these:

- a cell of the lesson that the build runs again;
- a curated reference of the register, an outbound link;
- a dataset card of the repository;
- a theorem that Lean checks;
- a recorded run of an agent that the build replays.

A claim without evidence, or with evidence that does not exist, stops the
build, so every row below has a target. The page is generated from the lessons
when the site is built. Where a statement quotes a value that the lesson
computes, the value is shown as "…"; the lesson has it.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pbc.authoring import evidence_page

print(evidence_page())
```
